description: Default reporting week starts on Monday. This is a product default, not a universal payroll rule. An overnight shift counts in the week of its start date
Gross pay before tax and deductions, from worker-confirmed hours and rates
break_minutes is deducted from paid hours
Overtime not applied in the MVP: every hour is paid at the standard rate. Weekly output also shows an overtime figure for comparison
Weekly hours above this are overtime when enabled
Rate multiplier for overtime hours when enabled
Longer shifts are flagged as invalid duration
Initial commute gap warning between shifts at different locations. This is a product default, not a universal travel time rule
Saturday and Sunday shifts are labelled weekend
Round money to 2 decimal places
Hourly rate is entered or confirmed by the worker
Cancelled shifts that were not worked are kept as records but not counted
Any pay for cancelled shifts needs separate rules and is outside the initial scope
The MVP is tested with csv input first
CSV comes first. PDF and image follow if time and reliability allow (Castro 2026-11-12)
break_minutes must be zero or more and shorter than the shift duration, otherwise the shift is flagged as invalid
Weekly totals are kept per currency and never added across currencies
A confirmed shift without a rate stays visible but is left out of gross pay and counted as incomplete

A missing employer or location is a warning and does not stop the shift counting, as long as the essential shift details are valid. A missing or unknown location means the commute check is unavailable, not passed
A missing date is a blocking validation error under the missing or invalid flag, with a specific missing date reason

needs_review shifts show in the review queue and are left out of final earnings until corrected and confirmed. Rejected shifts are kept for traceability but left out of the active schedule and earnings
Earnings are calculated from validated, worker-confirmed shift data, including the worker's corrections. The original csv stays available for traceability and comparison

A missing break is never treated as zero minutes. The shift stays visible and its earnings are incomplete until the worker confirms no break (0) or enters the break, so estimated earnings are not overstated
A possible duplicate is warned, and the extra copy is held for review and not counted. Final earnings never count the same shift twice before the worker resolves it
A missing currency makes that shift's earnings incomplete. No total is produced without a currency, and totals are never mixed across currencies
